title: Aaron Long books a trip to Jacksonville and Eagle Eye blocks them
summary: Aaron Long gives up his market to book the band to Jacksonville, hoping for Tampa and Miami, but Eagle Eye's band keeps them out of the Elks Hall.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So, uh, we stayed around there, I'd say, uh... Oh, let's see. I came back here, it was just before 27. Uh-huh. Well, the band made a big hit. Uh-huh. And we didn't have no particular man, we had this particular man, Aaron Long, I forgot to tell you. He booked us on a trip, he gave up his market, and booked us on a trip from Pensacola to Jacksonville. And the fellow, George Morris, we were not talking to Aaron Long, talking to the band members, he said, if we get to Jacksonville, he said, I know if we get down to Tampa and Panama for all, he said, we'd make some money. He said, I was down there as a cook. And he said, they don't have no New Orleans Tampa band down there. He said, we know what we did in this territory. So, we played this guy here along, he was, I think a Mason or something like that, he knew it was a different thing, we played, oh, I remember we played Tallahassee, I remember that, but we played other places on the way going to Jacksonville. And we didn't have too much hardship in the city of the band, because we always had a place to eat, sleep, and sometimes the money was short, sometimes, but it was always a proposition. We made, we got good, it was on a, what you call a percentage proposition, you see. So when we got to Jacksonville, Florida, the place that we were supposed to play, it was, I believe they called it the Elks Hall, and there was a band there called Eagle Eye, he was the leader of that band. And they wouldn't let us play that place.
